title: Customers
text: The customer record is where sales work starts. It holds the account details, the people you deal with, the deals you are chasing and a log of every call and email. Quotes, orders and invoices all hang off a customer, so a clean record here saves time everywhere else. Who can do this: See customers, the pipeline and follow-ups : sales representatives and managers, bookkeepers, billing clerks, finance approvers, plant managers, quality managers, executives, dispatchers and field technicians (permission "view customers"). Add or change customers, contacts, opportunities and activities : sales representatives, sales managers and bookkeepers (permission "manage customers"). Start a quote from a customer : sales representatives, sales managers and service dispatchers (permission "quote"). Find a customer Open Sales & supply → Customers . The page has three tabs: Customers , Pipeline and My follow-ups . On Customers , type part of a name or code into Search . Each row shows the code, name, type, industry, owner, how many opportunities are open and the date of the last activity. Click a row to open the customer. Type What it means Prospect Someone you are talking to who has not bought yet. Every new customer you add by hand starts here. Customer A prospect that has accepted a quote. The record changes to Customer by itself when you record the acceptance (see Quotes and orders ). Add a customer On the Customers page, click New customer . You only see the button if you can manage customers. Enter a Code (a short unique label such as ACME) and the Name . Both are required. Fill in Industry , Phone , Website and Billing address if you have them. Payment terms starts as Net 30 ; change it if this customer has different terms. New invoices and quotes take their terms from here. Click Save customer . The new record opens. If you already keep a customer list in a spreadsheet or another system, ask your administrator to bring it in with Data import instead of typing each one. See Importing data . Contacts, opportunities and activity The customer page is laid out in blocks. If you can manage customers, each block has a small form under its table. Contacts Under Contacts , enter the person's name (required), and optionally title, email and phone. Tick Primary for the person who should receive invoices and payment reminders. The reminder email on a receivable goes to the primary contact's email. Click Add contact . Opportunities An opportunity is a possible sale: a title, an amount, and the date you expect to close it. Under Opportunities , type a title (at least three letters), an amount and an expected close date. Click Add . It starts at the Lead stage. As the deal moves, pick the next stage in the row and click Move . If you choose Lost , type why in the Why lost? box. Stage Starting chance of winning Lead 10% Qualified 25% Proposal 50% Negotiation 75% Won 100% Lost 0% When you accept a quote that is linked to an opportunity, the opportunity moves to Won by itself. Won and lost opportunities no longer show a stage selector. Activity Use Activity to keep a record of what happened. Choose the kind ( Call , Email , Meeting , Note or Follow-up task ), write a short summary and click Log . A follow-up task also needs a due date. If the customer has an open opportunity you can tie the entry to it. The pipeline The Pipeline tab lists all open opportunities in four columns: Lead, Qualified, Proposal and Negotiation. The line above the columns shows how many are open, the total value, and the value weighted by probability : each amount multiplied by its chance of winning. Click a card to open its customer. My follow-ups The My follow-ups tab lists your open follow-up tasks with their due dates. Overdue ones have a red edge. Click Done when you have finished one. The task owner is also reminded when a follow-up falls due. Other things on the customer page Quotes and orders : lists of this customer's quotes and sales orders (Standard edition only). Click one to open it. New quote in the page header starts a quote for this customer. Specifications : if your company stores this customer's drawings or standards in document control, they are listed here with the revision currently in force. See Document control . Account : open invoices, payments, credit limit and exposure are on the customer's account page under Receivables. See Receivables . Lite and Standard Customers, contacts, opportunities and follow-ups work the same in both editions. In the Lite edition the quote and order blocks do not appear, because quotes, sales orders and shipments are part of Standard. Common mistakes Duplicate customers. Search by name before adding. Two records for the same company split their invoices and credit exposure. No primary contact. Without one, the Email payment reminder button on an invoice is unavailable. Forgetting to log a lost reason. The reason is the only record of why you did not win the work. Administrators can import customer lists and set credit limits and owners in bulk. Roles that may manage customers are set per role; see Roles and access and Importing data .

title: Quotes and orders
text: A quote is your written price to a customer. When the customer accepts it, you record that acceptance and the system turns the quote into a sales order. You then ship the order and invoice what shipped. This page walks through each step and what the statuses mean. Quotes, orders and shipments are part of the Standard edition. The Lite edition has customers and invoices but no quotes or orders. Who can do this: See quotes and orders : sales representatives and managers, plant managers, quality managers, finance approvers, billing clerks, bookkeepers, executives (permission "view sales"). Build, finish, send, revise, extend and record acceptance of quotes : sales representatives, sales managers and service dispatchers (permission "quote"). This is checked for the selling site. Add catalog items, set a promise date, ship, make : sales managers and plant or operations managers (permission "manage orders"). Approve out-of-limit pricing : the sales manager role, from the Approvals page. Release a credit hold : finance approvers (permission "release credit holds"). The sales catalog Open Sales & supply → Quotes & orders and click the Catalog tab. It lists the products and services you sell with their list price and standard cost. If you can manage orders, add one with the form under the table: code, description, Product or Service , list price, standard cost and, for a stocked product, the part it ships from. Quote lines can pick catalog items, which brings in the list price and cost so the system can check discount and margin. Build a quote Open the customer ( Customers ) and click New quote . You can also arrive here from a customer request ( Customer requests for quote ). Choose the Customer , enter a Title (at least three letters) and pick a Contact and, if one applies, an Opportunity . Choose the Selling site . Only sites where you may quote are offered. Set Valid until . If you leave it empty the quote is valid for 30 days from today. Under Lines , choose a catalog item or Not in the catalog (describe it) , then enter quantity and unit price. Leave the price empty to use the list price. A badge shows how far below list a line is. Click Add a line for more. Under Terms shown to the customer , fill in Lead time , Delivery , Included and Not included . Add Notes shown on the quote if needed. Click Save draft . Use Preview PDF on the next page to see the letter. The quote prints as a one-page letter with a validity banner, your terms, a signature block and page footers. Prices are stated excluding taxes. Tax and freight are not quote lines; they are added on the order's invoice. You can edit lines and terms while the quote is a draft ( Edit lines , Edit terms shown to the customer ). Once it has been finished, change it by making a new revision. Finish, approve and send On the quote, click Finish quote . The system checks the pricing. If every line is within 15% of list price and the margin on costed lines is at least 20%, the quote is ready to send. Otherwise a banner explains why, and the quote goes to a sales manager for Pricing approval . The manager decides from the Approvals page ( Home and approvals ). When the status is Ready to send , type the recipient in Send to (it defaults to the contact's email) and click Mark as sent (stores the PDF) . The system does not email the quote. Mark as sent freezes that revision, stores the exact PDF and logs the send on the customer. Open the PDF from the Sent table and send it yourself. The stored PDF is never changed afterward. Quote statuses Status Meaning What you can do Draft Being written. Edit lines and terms, then finish it. Pricing approval Outside the discount or margin limits; waiting for a sales manager. Wait, or start a new revision. Ready to send Pricing is cleared. Mark as sent, extend validity, or revise. Sent The customer has the PDF. Record acceptance or a decline, extend validity, or revise. Accepted The customer said yes; an order exists. Open the order. Declined The customer said no; the reason is kept. Start a new revision if they come back. Cancelled No longer going ahead. Nothing. Validity and expiry A red Expired badge appears next to a ready or sent quote whose Valid until date has passed. Expiry is worked out from the date; it is not a separate status. An expired quote cannot be accepted . Extend it or revise it first. On the quote list, the Validity filter shows Expiring within 7 days or Expired , and Time left counts the days. The quote owner is reminded 7 days before, 2 days before, and the day after a sent quote's expiry. Sent quotes that expired with no decision also appear on What is late . Extend a quote's validity On a quote that is Ready to send or Sent , set Extend validity to a date later than the current one. Type a Reason , such as "customer's budget approval pending". Click Extend . The old date, new date, reason, who and when are kept in Validity history , together with the original date. The PDF you already sent does not change; the customer's copy still shows the old date, so tell them in writing. Record the customer's acceptance When the customer says yes, open the sent quote. Under Record the customer's acceptance enter Accepted by (name) and Their title . Choose How they accepted : Purchase order , Signed quote , Email , Verbal or Customer portal . Set Date accepted . It cannot be in the future or before the quote was sent. Enter the Customer PO number . It is required when the method is Purchase order . Add a Note if they said something worth keeping, such as "ship in two lots". Click Customer accepted: create order . Then scan or upload the signed quote or PO under Files on the same page. The system records who, how, when, the revision and the total that was accepted, and creates the sales order from that revision. The opportunity moves to Won and the customer record becomes a customer. If the customer says no, type a reason in the box and click Customer declined . Revise a quote Type what change

text: A permission is one thing a person may do, such as approving a timesheet or releasing a production order. A role is a named bundle of permissions. This page lists all 89 permissions and, for each, the starter roles that hold it. It is generated from the product's permission list, so it matches what the system checks. How permissions work Every new company starts with 25 roles (listed below). The Administrator role holds every permission, including tenant.admin . A person is given a role at one site, on a group of sites, or at all sites (leave the site blank when granting). A permission only works at the sites where a role covering it was granted. See Sites and people and Roles and access . A person with several roles gets the combined permissions of all of them, site by site. Hiding a feature under Features removes that feature's permissions from the roles it is hidden from (the setting is cached for up to about 30 seconds). The permission is still in the role, but the system treats it as not held. Some actions are decided by a step in an approval chain rather than by a permission. Expenses and purchase requests are examples: the approver named in the rule can sign even without the matching manage permission. Nobody can approve their own timesheet or expense report (except in a single-person company where the licence allows it). The product has no screen for editing a role's permissions or adding a new role. Roles come from the starter list; the permission set of a role can only be changed by whoever operates the platform for you. Ask them if a starter role does not fit. To see what a particular person can do, add up the roles they were granted, then look each permission up here. The Administrator column is left out of the tables because the Administrator role holds everything.
